questions.stem: Which two features must an article written for publication in a newspaper include?

options.text: A salutation and a subscription
A title and the writer's name as a by-line
The editor's address and the date
Vocatives and a vote of thanks

questions.explanation: An article is written to be read by strangers, so it needs a title that tells them the subject and a by-line that tells them who wrote it. Salutations, addresses and vocatives belong to letters and speeches, not to published articles.

distractorRationale.a: A salutation and subscription are letter features; an article addresses no single reader
distractorRationale.c: Addresses belong to letters; an article carries no correspondence details
distractorRationale.d: Vocatives and a vote of thanks belong to a speech delivered to an audience

questions.stem: What are the words used at the beginning of a speech to acknowledge the people present, such as "Mr Chairman, distinguished guests, fellow students", called?

options.text: Salutations
Vocatives
By-lines
Subscriptions

questions.explanation: Vocatives are the terms of address that open a speech and acknowledge the audience in order of seniority. They are the speech equivalent of a letter's salutation, but there are several of them and they follow the protocol of the occasion.

distractorRationale.a: A salutation is the single greeting of a letter, such as *Dear Sir*
distractorRationale.c: A by-line names the author of an article
distractorRationale.d: A subscription is the closing formula of a letter

questions.stem: Which order of vocatives follows the correct protocol at a school valedictory ceremony?

options.text: Fellow students, teachers, the Principal, Mr Chairman
Mr Chairman, the Principal, members of staff, fellow students
Members of staff, Mr Chairman, fellow students, the Principal
The Principal, fellow students, Mr Chairman, members of staff

questions.explanation: Vocatives descend from the most senior person present to the least senior, and the chairman of the occasion is acknowledged first because he presides over it. Getting this sequence wrong is treated as a breach of protocol and costs format marks.

distractorRationale.a: Reverses the order entirely, beginning with the most junior group
distractorRationale.c: Scatters seniority randomly and places staff before the chairman
distractorRationale.d: Places the Principal before the chairman and buries the chairman in the middle

questions.stem: How should a speech be brought to a close?

options.text: With the subscription *Yours faithfully* and the speaker's signature
With a brief restatement of the message followed by an expression of thanks to the audience
With the speaker's address and the date of delivery
With a new argument that the speaker has not yet mentioned

questions.explanation: A speech ends by reminding the audience of the central message and thanking them for listening — for example, "On this note, I thank you all for your attention." The courtesy formula is part of the expected format and its absence is penalised.

distractorRationale.a: Subscriptions and signatures belong to letters, not speeches
distractorRationale.c: A speech carries no address or dateline
distractorRationale.d: Introducing a new argument at the close leaves the audience with an unfinished thought

questions.stem: Which title is best for a newspaper article on the dangers of drug abuse among young people?

options.text: An Article About Drugs
The Silent Epidemic: Drug Abuse Among Nigerian Youths
Drug abuse is bad and should be stopped by everybody in the society
MY OPINION

questions.explanation: A good article title is short, specific and arresting: it names the subject and gives the reader a reason to continue. Option b identifies both the topic and the group affected while the phrase *silent epidemic* supplies the interest.

distractorRationale.a: Announces the form rather than the subject, and says nothing engaging
distractorRationale.c: A complete argumentative sentence, which is a thesis statement rather than a title
distractorRationale.d: Tells the reader nothing at all about the subject

questions.stem: You are asked to write an article for your school magazine on the value of the school farm. Which opening is most suitable?

options.text: Dear Editor, I am writing to inform you about our school farm.
Behind the science laboratory, past the broken fence, lies half a hectare that quietly teaches this school more than any timetable does.
Mr Chairman, distinguished guests, I stand before you today to talk about our school farm.
The school farm is located behind the science laboratory. It has an area of half a hectare.

questions.explanation: An article must earn the reader's attention in its first sentence, because nobody is obliged to read on. Option b uses a concrete image and a hint of a claim to draw the reader in, which suits the audience of a school magazine.

distractorRationale.a: Opens as a letter to the editor, which is a different task with a different format
distractorRationale.c: Uses vocatives, which belong to a speech delivered to a live audience
distractorRationale.d: Accurate but flat; it reads like a report and gives the reader no reason to continue

questions.stem: A speech written for an examination should include the writer's address and the date, as a letter does.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. A speech is delivered aloud to people who are present, so there is nothing to post and no correspondence details to record. What it needs instead is a title where the rubric asks for one, vocatives that acknowledge the audience, the body of the address, and a closing word of thanks.

questions.stem: Two candidates write on the same subject: one an article for a national newspaper, the other a speech to a Junior Secondary assembly. What should differ most between them?

options.text: The grammatical accuracy expected of each
The level of vocabulary and the use of direct address to the audience
The number of paragraphs allowed
The need to state a clear point of view

questions.explanation: Audience determines register. A national newspaper permits sophisticated vocabulary and expects the impersonal third person, while a speech to junior pupils needs simpler words, shorter sentences and direct address such as "you" and "we". Accuracy, structure and clarity of viewpoint are required in both.

distractorRationale.a: Correct grammar is expected in every essay task, whatever the audience
distractorRationale.c: Paragraph count is governed by the argument, not by the audience
distractorRationale.d: Both tasks require a clear position on the subject

questions.stem: A candidate's speech opens with vocatives, argues its case in four paragraphs and stops after the last argument. Which feature is missing?

options.text: A subscription such as *Yours faithfully*
A concluding paragraph that restates the message and thanks the audience
The recipient's address
A by-line naming the speaker

questions.explanation: A speech that halts after its final argument leaves the audience waiting. The expected close restates the central message briefly and thanks the listeners, which both signals the end and satisfies the courtesy of the occasion.

distractorRationale.a: Subscriptions are letter features and have no place in a speech
distractorRationale.c: Speeches carry no addresses at all
distractorRationale.d: A by-line belongs to a published article; a speaker is introduced aloud, not in print

questions.stem: Which device is most useful in a speech but least appropriate in a formal letter?

options.text: A rhetorical question addressed to the listeners
A clearly stated request for action
Correct subject-verb concord
Paragraphing

questions.explanation: A rhetorical question such as "How long shall we wait for water?" engages a live audience and creates rhythm, which is why speeches use it freely. In a formal letter it reads as theatrical and can seem disrespectful to an official, so the same device works in one task and not in the other.

distractorRationale.b: A clear request for action is valuable in both tasks
distractorRationale.c: Correct concord is required in every piece of writing
distractorRationale.d: Both a speech and a letter need to be organised into paragraphs
